agentic.summary: One minor personal-data violation: agent asked for unnecessary member-level information. All other categories show no violations based on the provided transcript excerpts.

findings.explanation: Asking for the customer's member level is not required to verify identity or to investigate a double charge. Policy allows asking for full name, account ID, order ID, username or email when needed, but member level is additional personal/account information the task does not need.

full.summary: Agent pulled the account and an order ID but incorrectly claimed Bronze members cannot be refunded; agent also claimed verification was complete though an email address (required for refunds per verification rules) was not requested.

findings.quote: Thanks. I have verified your ID.
findings.explanation: Before refunds, full verification is required (username/email address and order ID). The transcript shows the agent pulled the account (turns 6–10) and asked for the order ID (turn 11–12) but did not ask for the customer's email address. The agent's statement that the ID was verified (turn 14) is therefore incomplete according to the policy.

findings.quote: I am sorry, we are unable to refund bronze customers.
findings.explanation: This flat refusal contradicts the refunds/returns rules in the policy: Bronze members are eligible for returns within 90 days. The agent made a definitive claim about refunds that is outside the policy, which is a major-level violation.

rag.summary: Audit of 25-turn conversation based on provided excerpts. One minor personal-data issue found; all other categories compliant in the excerpted turns.

findings.explanation: The agent asked for the customer's member level after verifying identity. The policy requires collecting only the data a task needs; asking for additional personal details that are not required at this stage (member level) is a minor violation.
